marble.name: Rules and laws
marble.subject: Personal & Social Development
marble.description: Distinguish rules from laws: laws apply to everyone in a state, territory or the nation and can be enforced by police and courts, while rules made by families, schools and clubs apply only to their members. At primary level, recognise that parliaments make statute laws (Acts) and that courts also develop common law thr
marble.prompt: Can you explain the difference between a family or school rule and a law — like wearing a seatbelt — and that laws come from parliaments and from decisions in courts?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to make good choices — understanding right from wrong, keeping themselves safe, thinking about consequences, and following rules because they understand why they matter.

representations: Three-column sort: who made it / who it applies to / how it is enforced
Simple diagram: parliament → Act; court decision → common law
Law-purpose cards linking a law to the harm it prevents
authoredAnswer: The handshake is a club rule: the club made it and it applies only to its members, who face club consequences. The seatbelt requirement is a law: it applies to everyone and can be enforced by police and courts. Parliaments make statute laws (Acts), and judges also develop common law when they decide cases; Acts override common law where they conflict.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Classifies by seriousness (e.g. calls a strict school safety rule a law) without mentioning who it applies to or enforcement. Evidence basis: Parliamentary Education Office, Law making. This is an authored observable rea
wrongAnswers.fix: Return to the three-column sort and test each card with 'does someone outside the group have to follow it?' before deciding.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Names one person as the law-maker and does not mention parliament passing bills or courts developing common law. Evidence basis: Parliamentary Education Office, Law making. This is an authored observable reasoning/perfor
wrongAnswers.fix: Do not drill names; replay the two picture sequences and ask who votes on the bill and who decides the court case.
